gen-dafont-disorder-lora: Chaotic and raw, Disorder scatters big-looking lowercase letters far apart in a wire-thin line. Lora, a text serif, is the opposite: sturdy hairlines, restrained thick strokes, and a welcoming c.
gen-dafont-disorder-noto-serif: Disorder draws hollow, glass-tube letters of constant thickness, set well apart and tall in the lowercase, with a raw, chaotic look. Noto Serif swells and thins gently beneath.
gen-dafont-dited-author: Author carries a refined, dignified voice, with a slight swell on its bowls that feels comfortable in small doses. Dited, wide and open on its round letters, earns its place big and short.
gen-dafont-dited-fs-bespoke-serif: Bespoke Serif looks authoritative, its thin strokes about half the weight of its thick ones. Bespoke Serif isn't meant for long paragraphs, while Dited sits tight on the line with a digital edge.
gen-dafont-dited-fs-erode: Crisp and digital, Dited packs its shapes hip to hip while Erode's tall middle band keeps shallow ascenders. Dited is best loud and tight; Erode is best when it flows.
gen-dafont-dited-fs-karma: Dited has a digital, tech feel, with letters tight on the line and round shapes opening wide. And Karma, a classic serif, trades that for trustworthy, quiet modulation that never snags the eye.
gen-dafont-dited-fs-sentient: Sentient reads sophisticated and contemporary, with pinched apertures and crossbars a touch thinner than its stems, made for short stretches of reading. And Dited adds a tech edge, tight on the line yet wide in its curves.
gen-dafont-dogica-lora: Heavy and blunt, Dogica lets its lowercase climb close to the capitals with wide tracking. Lora, a literary serif, follows with a modest dip in its thin strokes, softening the page.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-lora: Early GameBoy is commanding and playful, its extended tracking pushing a skyward x-height across the line. But Lora is the one for bookish ease, with a moderate lowercase and a broad, welcoming c.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-noto-serif: Noto Serif reads universal and literary, with a prominent x-height. Under Early GameBoy's wide, playful capitals, its subtle thick and thin cadence would carry a text serif page along comfortably, line after line.
